scope_boundaries: Bounded mass and a fixed smooth big background remain chapter premises.
The complete metric is constructed on all ordinary models with individually positive lower volume; no common cutoff defines its full domain.
Metric convergence and upper-volume-comparison convergence agree at every positive-volume model.
The metric has a stronger global Cauchy condition: reciprocal lower volumes must be Cauchy. On every fixed closed positive-lower-volume sector the comparisons are uniformly equivalent.
The original upper-volume formula fails the triangle inequality even on positive-volume analytic models in a closed Kahler background.
The positive-volume ideal models are a complete closed subspace and the completion of positive-volume analytic models for this metric.

No zero-lower-volume, infinite-mass or background-degeneration extension is asserted. The dyadic choices define a compatible complete metric; no canonical numerical formula or isometry with another metric is claimed.
